page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.large is a general-purpose cloud instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and ARMv9-based Neoverse-V2 architecture. It features 2 dedicated physical cores (2 vCPUs) clocked at 2.8 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core configuration. The CPU cache architecture includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. Memory is configured at 8.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes a dedicated 118 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume, baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and no discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent single-threaded execution across general computing tasks. Geekbench single-core reaches 1810.0, stress-ng single-core reports 1707.39, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression performs strongly at 14.13 GB/sec, placing in the top 25%. However, overall aggregate throughput is constrained by the small 2-core footprint. Geekbench multi-core registers 3234.0, stress-ng multi-core yields 3403.17, and PassMark CPU score falls into the bottom 10% at 1986.08. Text processing (2095.0) and PassMark database operations (3023.03) score within the average tier, while static web serving throughput measures 5.11 GB/sec.

Memory bandwidth tests show 56.19 GB/sec for uncached read-only large blocks in the middle 50% tier, though cached small-block reads (230.48 GB/sec) and large-block writes (22.47 GB/sec) measure in the lower 25%. Redis SET performance delivers 4.67 million operations per second. Machine learning capabilities are restricted by CPU-only execution and core count, resulting in 145.92 tokens per second for prompt processing and 68.34 tokens per second for generation on small 135M parameter models, with no support for medium or large models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the inclusion of dedicated ARM cores and direct-attached NVMe storage provides solid utility for workloads requiring fast local scratch storage without relying exclusively on remote block storage volumes. Tradeoffs include low absolute multi-threaded throughput and lack of AVX or x86 instruction sets. AWS m8gd.large is primarily fitted for lightweight web services, caching tiers, edge microservices, local build tasks, and small transactional databases requiring fast NVMe I/O.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gd.large is a general-purpose ARMv9 instance based on the AWS Neoverse-V2 architecture and managed by the Nitro hypervisor. The instance provides 2 dedicated physical cores operating at 2.8 GHz, 8.0 GB of system memory, and a bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD instance store, paired with 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Single-threaded metrics are solid, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1810.0 and bzip3 decompression reaching 14.13 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is naturally constrained by the dual-core profile, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 3234.0 and PassMark CPU score of 1986.08. With 4.67 million Redis SET operations per second and average database operation performance, m8gd.large represents a cost-efficient resource tier for lightweight web serving, caching, small database workloads, and application components requiring fast local NVMe storage.
